notes.decision: Lycopolitan feminine ordinal: ⲧ-ⲧ-ⲙⲁⲍ-ⲙⲛⲧⲥⲛⲁⲩⲥ = 'the twelfth.' Standard ordinal-prefix ⲙⲁⲍ- with cardinal ⲙⲛⲧⲥⲛⲁⲩⲥ '12.'

Identifies the twelfth judge (Counsel) AS the Call+Hearing pair, set within the elements. The twelfth judge = the cosmic Call/Answer dyad embedded in stoicheia. Direct correspondential identification per Manichaean exegesis.

Read as 'depicting himself by himself.' ⲍⲱⲣⲁⲫⲉ from ζωγραφέω 'paint, depict from life' (already in glossary). The ⲛ̄ϩ- prefix functions as circumstantial/participial. The cosmic Image self-depicting at the eschatological gathering.

ⲡⲁⲛⲁⲣⲉⲓⲁⲥ = ἀναίρεσις 'extraction, lifting-out, destruction' (per glossary). 'The destruction/lifting-out of the end' — the eschatological extraction of light at the cosmic terminus. Translated 'Pan-areias' to highlight the Greek loan; could equally be 'in the destruction.'
ⲛⲉⲉϩ = ⲛⲉⲉϥ 'bears up, sustains' (per glossary). The hidden Father bears up all twelve judges as Atlas-figure of the entire judicial structure.

Apophatic privative compound: ⲁⲧ- ('un-') + ⲧⲱⲙⲉ ('touch') + -ⲁⲣⲁϩ ('to him'). 'Untouchable to him' — characteristic Manichaean apophatic epithet of the hidden Father. ⲧⲱⲙⲉ already in vocabulary as 'touch/join.'
= ⲙⲛⲧϣⲙⲏⲛ 'eight' (cardinal-abstract). Lyc. ⲝ for ⲧϣ regular dialectal sandhi. Chapter heading: 'the Eight Great Thrones of all the Fathers.'
= ⲥⲟⲟⲩ 'six' (Lyc. ϯⲥ regular). Six of the eight thrones are set in the outer aeons; by implication two remain in the inner Greatness — the first being the Father's throne (line 29ff).

Translated tentatively 'the Half (Region).' ⲡⲁⲥⲉ may be Lyc. ⲡⲁϣ 'half, division' or a specific cosmological region. The phrase 'in all the worlds of ⲡⲁⲥⲉ' designates the cosmological domain in which the six outer thrones reside. Confidence low; flag for parallels.

'In his own essence, by himself.' ⲟⲩⲥⲓⲁ = οὐσία (per terminology guide: 'substance/essence'). Here in apophatic context of the Father's throne: he sits alone in his own substance, by himself, upon himself — the absolute self-grounding of the divine throne.
ⲟⲩⲁⲧⲃⲉ from ⲟⲩⲱⲧⲃ 'pass over, surpass, transcend' (cf. ⲟⲩⲱⲑ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ in glossary). The first throne is 'the one which surpasses all (other) thrones' — hierarchic supremacy of the Father's throne.
